blurb: Fluffy white spitz in three sizes, descended from German Spitz and once a circus star
description: The American Eskimo Dog is a white spitz companion dog of German Spitz descent, bred in the US in toy, miniature and standard sizes with a thick coat.
answer: The American Eskimo Dog is a spitz-type companion dog developed in the United States from German Spitz brought by European immigrants, and renamed during the era of World War I. It comes in toy, miniature and standard sizes, from about 22 to 50 cm tall, and typically lives around 12 to 14 years.

body: European immigrants brought spitz dogs to the United States, especially New York, in the early 1900s. White was the preferred colour in the US, and anti-German sentiment around World War I led owners to call them American Spitz and later American Eskimo. The dogs became popular circus performers in the 1930s and 1940s, and many of today's dogs trace back to circus lines. Japanese Spitz may have been crossed in after World War II.

The United Kennel Club recognised the breed in 1919. The National American Eskimo Dog Association was founded in 1970, and the American Kennel Club recognised the breed in 1995 from a base of 1,750 pedigreed dogs.

American Eskimo Dogs are usually white, though white and biscuit is also accepted by the AKC. They have a thick, straight double coat with a ruff around the neck and shoulders and a heavily furred tail that usually curls over the back. Size varieties are toy (22 to 30 cm, 2.3 to 4.5 kg), miniature (30 to 40 cm, 4.5 to 9 kg) and standard (38 to 50 cm, 6.8 to 18 kg).

The source text gives little detail on temperament. The breed has traditionally served as a watchdog and companion, and its circus history reflects an aptitude for learning tricks; breed clubs give fuller descriptions of its character.
Sources give little specific care guidance. A thick double coat is generally expected to need regular brushing, and exercise needs are likely to vary with the size variety.

faq.q: How big does an American Eskimo Dog get?
faq.a: It depends on the variety: toys are about 22 to 30 cm, miniatures about 30 to 40 cm and standards about 38 to 50 cm at the withers.

faq.q: How long do American Eskimo Dogs live?
faq.a: Typical life expectancy is about 12 to 14 years.

faq.q: Is the American Eskimo Dog the same as a German Spitz?
faq.a: It descends from the German Spitz, but the two have diverged and their standards are now significantly different.
